audit.whatIsWrong: Row 6 gave the two-item stage to Irelia while whys[6], spikes[3] and the late paragraph all say a reset-starved Irelia falls off and you out-scale her. Row 4 sat on 'Skill' against the mirror. The whys were also shifted a stage: whys[4], on the Level 6 row, talked about her item spike.
audit.why: The mirror audit on irelia__vladimir set row 4 to Irelia and row 6 to Vladimir. That gives Irelia levels 2-3, level 6 and her first item — the 46.59% window — and hands you the two-item stage, which is what all of your own late-game prose describes.
audit.corrected: Rows 4 and 6 flipped as matched win[N] + phases[N].side pairs, phases[6].rating rescaled, and whys[4] and whys[5] rewritten so each row's explanation belongs to that row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. Flawless Duet is named on eight fields without a single number.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 and Vanguard's Edge 125/105/85, so at rank 1 a dodged E buys you a full 16 seconds. Bladesurge is 10s down to 6s but refreshes outright if the target is Marked or dies to it, so its printed cooldown is not what you play around — the wave is.
audit.corrected: Sequencing written into dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[1].d and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single biggest interaction in this matchup was absent: Defiant Dance reduces only physical damage, so it does nothing against Vladimir's entirely magic kit.
audit.why: Riot's text says 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Vladimir deals magic damage with Transfusion, Tides of Blood and Hemoplague, so her defensive charge is a free window for you rather than a reason to hold poke. The Bladesurge refresh condition — Marked target or a kill — was also missing.
Bladesurge heals her on every dash, so Grievous Wounds decides extended trades — report[8].t already carries the early anti-heal buy.

notes: Defiant Dance being physical-only is the highest-value fact on this page and it was nowhere: a Vladimir has no reason to hold poke through her W charge. Left alone, as the mirror did: the derived grounding flag on Flawless Duet contradicts Riot's description, which mentions only damage, stun and Mark — I did not assert grounding in either direction.
